sentences.text: Arganasuchus is an extinct genus of rauisuchian archosaur that contains only one known species, Arganasuchus dutuiti.
Its upper jaw features a distinctive Y-shape with an unusually long anterior process, holding at least twelve large, knife-like teeth in deep sockets.
Preserved fragments of the front jaw suggest the animal possessed at least fourteen teeth in its lower jaw.
The pubis bone is considered one of the most unusual skeletal features, defined by the unique size and orientation of the acetabulum.
Large, knife-shaped teeth indicate that this predator was a carnivore.
A smaller knob on the femur may indicate diseased bone, offering a rare glimpse into the animal's health.
Jean-Michel Dutuit first reported fossils in 1979, initially attributing them to Ticinosuchus before they were identified as a distinct genus in 2007.
The species exhibited an alternating tooth replacement scheme common among archosaurs.
Arganasuchus belongs to the family Rauisuchidae and is universally classified as a rauisuchian.
The group Rauisuchia is currently viewed as a paraphyletic grade of archosaurs rather than a natural clade.
This animal is classified within the class Reptilia.
Fossils were found in the Timezgadiouine Formation in the Argana Basin of Morocco, dated to the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic.
Arganasuchus lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during this period.
It is debated how Arganasuchus fits into modern crocodilian ancestry classifications, leaving its precise relationship to other rauisuchians poorly understood.
There is no scientific consensus on the precise phylogenetic affinities of Arganasuchus despite various analytical attempts.
